$comment: Life events with friends ({name}: someone you know who is with you) and family (children, pets).

events.title: The birthday you missed
events.prompt: "Good weekend?" asks {name}. "It was my birthday, actually." Oh no.

outcomes.text: You apologise properly, no excuses. {name} waves it off, but they're smiling now.
You drag them for lunch and make the staff sing. {name} wants to die. {name} also loves it.
Somehow they buy it. You now owe them a surprise.
{name} just looks at you until you crack. "Okay. I forgot."

events.title: Do you own a van?
events.prompt: {name} is moving on Saturday. "It's just a few boxes," they say. It is never just a few boxes.

outcomes.text: It is forty-one boxes and a piano. You are owed pizza for life.

memory.text: Helped {name} move. There was a piano.

outcomes.text: "I'd love to, but my cousin…" You don't have a cousin. {name} knows you don't have a cousin.
You send encouraging memes all Saturday. {name} sends back a photo of the piano.

events.title: The voice
events.prompt: {name} does The Voice. The one from that night. You haven't been able to breathe properly for a minute.

outcomes.text: You do it back. You both slide off your seats. Strangers look concerned.
"That's getting old." It isn't. You both know it isn't.

events.title: Did you hear?
events.prompt: {name} leans in, delighted. "Did you hear about what happened at the Copper Tap last night?"

outcomes.text: It's a good story. It's possibly a true story. You feel closer, and slightly worse.
You ask about their week instead. {name} looks briefly cheated, then tells you about their week.
"Whatever it was, leave them be." {name} goes quiet. They'll remember you said it.

events.title: A quiet evening
events.prompt: It's that hour of the evening where everyone else seems to be somewhere, with someone.

outcomes.text: You put shoes on before you can talk yourself out of it. Half the battle; maybe all of it.
You cook properly, light a candle, and eat at the table like a person in a film about getting their life together.
You lie on the floor and listen to sad songs. Honestly, sometimes it helps.

events.title: Where do the stars go?
events.prompt: At bedtime your child asks, very seriously, where the stars go in the daytime.

outcomes.text: You explain that they're still there, just outshone. Your child thinks about it. "Like you at parties." Wow.

memory.text: Explained the stars to my child at bedtime.

outcomes.text: You invent the Star Keepers, who fold them away each morning. You will be asked for this story every night for a year.

memory.text: Made up the Star Keepers at bedtime.

outcomes.text: "Ask me tomorrow." They will. They absolutely will.

events.title: The crime scene
events.prompt: Your favourite shoes. What's left of them. Your pet is sitting next to the evidence, looking proud.

choices.label: Laugh. What else can you do?

outcomes.text: You laugh until your eyes water and take a photo for posterity. The shoes are gone, but the photo is great.

memory.text: My pet ate my favourite shoes.

outcomes.text: You deliver a long, serious lecture. Your pet listens intently and learns absolutely nothing.

events.title: A masterpiece
events.prompt: A drawing has appeared on the fridge: a tall wobbly person holding a small wobbly person's hand. The tall one is labelled with your name.

outcomes.text: You frame it. It's the most valuable thing you own and it's worth nothing to anyone else.

memory.text: Framed my child's drawing of the two of us.

outcomes.text: It's your lock screen now. You look at it during every meeting.
